archetype.name: Fallen Contender (offense in free fall)
archetype.definition: A team coming off a run of winning seasons, including 14 wins in 2024 and 11 in 2025, whose efficiency has collapsed to the bottom of the league behind a line that can't block and a three-quarterback carousel.

report.headline: Two wins unlucky, but the efficiency says this collapse is mostly real.
report.take:
This is not a rebuilding roster. The Eagles won 14 games in 2024 with the 3rd-best net EPA in football and were still a top-10 defense by EPA last year. That makes 2-7 and 31st in net EPA so jarring. The record is not a mirage either: they sit 29th in point differential per game, 30th in offensive EPA and last in yards per game. Their two wins came by two and four points over Washington and Tennessee in the first fortnight, and they haven't won since.

The engine failure is up front. Philadelphia is stuffed on 29.8% of runs, the worst rate in the league, averages 3.16 yards a carry (30th) and gets 2.1 yards before contact (29th). The passers have taken 30 sacks, 30th in the league. That has buried a backfield where Saquon Barkley has 69 carries in seven games. It has also made life miserable for three different starting quarterbacks: Jalen Hurts for six starts, Tanner McKee for two, and Joe Milton III in Week 9, when the offense posted -16.9 passing EPA and took seven sacks. The defense is closer to ordinary than bad. It ranks 18th in points allowed and 14th in red-zone TD rate. But it barely pressures the quarterback (26th in pressure rate, 30th in QB-hit rate) and has the fewest takeaways in the league, so it never hands the offense a short field.

What the numbers hide: some of this is bad luck in the margins. Wins over expected is -2.1 (31st), and the point differential implies 4.1 wins rather than two. Sirianni has also kept attacking, going for it on every fourth-down chance he's judged go-worthy (1st). The Book, though, has been slow to catch up. Philadelphia has covered only 11.1% of its games, missing even as a 6- and 7-point favorite in the two wins. The reputation is still being priced in, not the team on the field.

There is a precedent in the history. In 2020 the Eagles went 4-11 with wins over expected of -2.62 and a bottom-five turnover margin, then bounced back. A softer patch of the schedule is coming after Pittsburgh: Dallas (31st-ranked defense), Arizona (29th) and 2-7 Indianapolis. But DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks are both listed out, and the quarterback situation is unresolved. Expect a few more wins and better luck in close games, not a turnaround.

strengths.title: Record undersells the point margin
strengths.body: The scoreboard implies about two more wins than Philadelphia has. Wins over expected ranks 31st, and they are 0.4 in one-score games. Close-game results tend to even out, so some positive regression in the record is likely even if the underlying play doesn't improve much.

strengths.title: Fourth-down aggression hasn't wavered
strengths.body: Even in a lost season the staff goes for it on fourth down more readily than anyone in the league. For an offense that struggles to string together drives, that is the right call: it squeezes extra possessions out of the few drives that do get going. It is a coaching trait, so it should hold.

strengths.title: Defense holds the line near the goal
strengths.body: The defense bends, but it doesn't break more than average. It is mid-pack in red-zone TD rate and run yards allowed per game, and it has held opposing tight ends well under their norms. That keeps games closer than the yardage suggests, though it is a floor, not a strength to build on.

concerns.title: Line can't run block or protect
concerns.body: This is the root problem. Philadelphia has the league's worst stuff rate and gets little push before contact. Its quarterbacks are sacked at a bottom-eight rate. The quarterback churn makes the sacks worse, but the run-game numbers show it is a front-five problem first, and that rarely gets fixed in-season.

concerns.title: Passing game lost its pieces
concerns.body: The passing offense ranks 27th in EPA. It has now cycled through Hurts, McKee and Milton, and the Week 9 start was the low point. Two of the top four targeted receivers, Smith and Wicks, are listed out. That leaves rookie-year volume leader Makai Lemon, Dallas Goedert and Darius Cooper to carry it.

concerns.title: No pressure, no takeaways
concerns.body: The defense ranks last in takeaways and 26th in pressure rate, which combine for a 28th-ranked turnover margin. Without disruption it can't steal possessions for a struggling offense. The six-sack game against the Giants was the exception, not the pattern.

trend.note: A 2-0 start built on narrow wins over weak Washington and Tennessee offenses gave way to a winless stretch that included 17-point losses to Dallas and Washington. The Week 9 loss to the Giants, with seven sacks taken and -16.9 passing EPA, was the offense's worst passing showing yet.

nextGame.headline: Worst run defense meets the league's best ground game.
nextGame.body:
Pittsburgh arrives at 6-2 with a top-six defense by EPA and an offense that is all ground game: 1st in rush EPA, 2nd in yards per carry, 1st on short yardage, but 26th in pass EPA. Philadelphia's defense is 31st in rush EPA allowed, and that collision is where this game tilts. On the other side, the Steelers' pass rush ranks 4th in sack rate against an Eagles line that just allowed seven sacks. The openings are in the Pittsburgh secondary: it ranks 23rd on deep passes and 30th in EPA allowed to tight ends. The Steelers' 6-2 also carries some luck, with 1.6 wins over expected and an 0.8 win rate in one-score games. No line is posted yet. The Eagles come in off a bye, with 14 days of rest.

Availability is the bigger story for Philadelphia. DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks and linebacker Jihaad Campbell were all listed out, with return estimates that land on game day, so treat each as uncertain. Zack Baun, a 93%-snap linebacker, is questionable with a back injury, and corners Michael Carter II and Jonathan Jones are also out. The dossier doesn't say who starts at quarterback after Milton's Week 9 start. Pittsburgh has had Aaron Rodgers for every start. Its WR Michael Pittman Jr. is on IR with no clear activation timeline, DT Sebastian Joseph-Day is on IR, and two depth corners are out.

waysToWin.title: Feed Goedert against a leaky middle
waysToWin.body: Pittsburgh allows the second-most EPA per play in the league to tight ends. With Smith and Wicks possibly out, Goedert is the natural first read. Quick throws to him also beat the pass rush to the punch, which this line badly needs.

waysToWin.title: Take shots over the top
waysToWin.body: The Steelers are stingy underneath but rank 23rd on deep passes and 22nd in explosive pass rate allowed. If protection holds for a handful of snaps, one or two chunk plays could decide a low-scoring game.

waysToWin.title: Win the hidden yards
waysToWin.body: Pittsburgh is 23rd in special-teams EPA, while Philadelphia is mid-pack and far more willing to go for it on fourth down. Field position and extra possessions are how a weaker team stays in a game against a ball-control opponent.

waysToLose.title: Steelers grind it out on the ground
waysToLose.body: The league's most efficient rushing offense meets a run defense ranked 31st in EPA. Pittsburgh is 6th in time of possession, and Philadelphia is 31st. If the Steelers stay on schedule, the Eagles' offense may get only a handful of drives.

waysToLose.title: Pass rush swamps the pocket again
waysToLose.body: Pittsburgh's sack rate is 4th in the league, and Philadelphia's line allows sacks at a bottom-eight rate. That line just gave up seven sacks to the Giants. Drive-killing sacks on early downs are the likeliest way this offense stalls out.

waysToLose.title: Red-zone trips end in field goals
waysToLose.body: The Steelers allow touchdowns on just 37.5% of red-zone trips, 3rd-best in the league, and they force turnovers at a top-10 clip. An offense this inefficient can't afford to trade touchdowns for kicks or to give the ball away.

nextGame.watch: Who takes the first snap at quarterback, and whether the line can keep Pittsburgh's rush from turning early downs into sacks.

restOfSeason.body:
The schedule opens up after Pittsburgh. Dallas and Arizona both field bottom-four defenses by EPA, and Indianapolis is 2-7 with the 30th-ranked offense. That stretch, plus some regression in a 0.4 one-score win rate, should produce a few more wins. The ceiling is capped by things that don't regress: the worst stuff rate in the league, a bottom-tier sack rate and a defense that neither pressures nor takes the ball away. Seattle's 5th-ranked defense, San Francisco's top offense and a road trip to the Giants make the back end hard.

What's sustainable is mediocrity, not this level of misery. The defense should keep allowing points at a mid-pack rate. The offense moves only if a quarterback sticks and Smith and Wicks return. If the carousel keeps spinning, the passing EPA from the Giants game is a warning of how low it can go.
swingFactors: Smith and Wicks returning from injury

confidence.note: Nine games is a real sample, but the quarterback is unsettled and key receivers are out.
